Here is the list of songs Lou adores singing on stage. Along as how she feels regarding them:

- "Tina Turner - the best": *this is a song she adores to sing in front of an audience, most often taking someone from the audience and bringing it on stage as to address the song as if she meant the lyrics personally*.

- "Patricia Kaas - mon mec à moi": *so far, It is maybe Lou's favorite song to sing in front of an audience, she also most often daydreams a bit during her performance, as it is actually how she idealizes the male of her dreams. Canonically when Ifri Léna and Susan meets up at La Fourrure, she is singing this song in front of the stage before coming over saying hi to the two anthros.

- "Madonna - love don't live here anymore": *It is a difficult heartbreaking song; in fact, it is most often a song that brings her to tears while singing as it reminds her of the abrupt breakup she had with the father of her first cubs. She never sings this song on stage except if she feels very sad, or got very drunk on whiskey during the night.*

- "Amy Winehouse - Back to black": *once again a breakup song, surprisingly it's a song that doesn't affect her much than this. She generally sings it on stage for someone that lived a breakup recently.*

-"Tori Amos - Raspberry Swirl": *Lou started to add this song to her repertoire when her eldest daughter, Alice, actually came out as being lesbian. She sings this song on stage a bit as a hommage, keeping the reason secret of why she has it in her repertory.*

- "Vonda Shepard - I know him by heart": *she generally concludes her stage performance with this song. She feels quite melancholic, but hopeful and contemplative while singing it.*

- "Dolly Parton - I will always love you": *it's not her favorite song, but every once in a while she doesn't dislike to sing it. As much as she actually adores Whitney Houston's version, she's actually not capable of matching such keynotes, the chorus becoming a sort of scrambled howl the only time she tried as a challenge because one of her children asked to try. So it's a song she generally sings in a soft tone so to not force on her vocal chords, she's unsure whether the public would like if she would push in the octaves (personally she doesn't really like the recording of the time she tried, despite she got good returns of it every now and then).*

- "Niagara - Encore un dernier baiser": *as surprising as it seems despite the title, it's really not a breakup song but actually a making out song, the singer in the song asking for a last kiss to her lover before making love, the last kiss basically symbolising the start of foreplaying. Lou actually likes the atmosphere of the song, as it is very cabaret, it is also one of the favorites of La Fourrure's regulars, and she doesn't get bored singing it in front of the audience.*

- "Niagara - Tchiki Boum": *it is once again one of the favorite songs from the regulars of La Fourrure, very blue-flower, very cabaret-like (La Fourrure is a cabaret after all), the song is about a woman fantasizing of being raptured by her lover, submitting to his will. Lou sings it in duet with a male singer part of the staff of La Fourrure. Despite the underlying theme, this is a song that doesn't really speak much to her, being a bit too human-centered for her to enjoy in terms of point of view. Ironically this song makes her think about her younger sister Manuella for some reason she can't really seem to point out.*

- "Niagara - L'amour à la plage": *L'amour à la plage is a song about a summer love. But it is most importantly one of La Fourrure's most famous numeros, in which a stage representing a beach and a bar cabin in the pacific is being set up, the staff members being respectively in bikini for the females and in bermuda for the males. She makes of the several people that sings it during the numero, Lou is singing a few lines along as doing the 'aooh, aooh' backing vocals of this song. In this numero Lou wears a large two piece bikini of green color with a Aloha-shirt-like print.*

- "France Gall - La Déclaration d'Amour": *It is one of Lou's favorite songs to sing, despite her cover version differs quite a lot (France Gall actually had a mezzo tone of voice, much higher-pitched than Lou's Contralto voice tone), it is a bit more slower paced than the original version (while the original version was already more or less of a slow) and maybe also much more intimate and decisive in terms of interpretation, as if the declaration was really being made and she was meaning it, but wanted to take her time to express it in the best manner, taking time for things to unfold.

- "Jeanne Mas - Ideali": *This is a very intimate song to her, in fact this is a very melancholic song to her as she finds it to describe the relationship dynamic she has with her elder sister Katherine. It is a song that often leaves her vulnerable. So she prefers to sing it as the last song before the mid-break so she can go drink a glass of liquor after she finished so to cheer up and continue the spectacle.*

entries.name: Katherine Béa
entries.content: Katherine is Lou's older sister, she's only older than Lou by a few minutes. Lou don't like much Katherine as their relationship always been conflictual. Katherine always been more or less of a bully to Lou. Lou also don't like much that Katherine is very predatory to anyone and everyone, including Lou's own children. She tries to protect her children a maximum from Katherine, especially her boys. Lou is generally very calm as a person, but she can get very agressive and angry when it touches to her flesh and blood, as a result, Lou can be rather short-tempered when she interacts with Katherine.
